annotations.title: Read one whole MFM market (open data)

description: Read in ONE request every aggregated series MFM publishes for one market, from the open data (free to download, also as CSV at /open-data/): the basket of Observatory companies of the index (price on base 100 at its first month, prices only; basket_gap = basket price ÷ its bottom-up long-term part − 1, same companies on both sides), the Market Weather month by month (grade, family readings, company aggregates) and, for the United States, the S&P 500 sector gaps. Markets with a basket: US (S&P 500), EU (STOXX Europe 600), JP (Japan), CH (Switzerland); other Weather markets have only the Weather series. No company page and no quota consumed. The top-down series (value from the top, its gap, the band) and index levels are not included (licensed inputs). Provisional months (rule P1: official company prices not public yet) have no basket price and an empty basket_gap, with a reason that starts with «Provisional month»; their bottom-up gap in whole percent, with its measured error and the date by which the official prices are expected, is in /data/valori/<cc>.json (rows with provisional true) and in long_term_calculator (provisional_months). Items under licence (company prices of the most recent months, index levels, index earnings, index constituent lists) are not redistributed: you can combine MFM data with data you obtain from other sources, whose terms of use are the user's responsibility. Optional since=YYYY-MM shortens the series; include chooses the blocks. Past data only: no forecast, no expected return, no advice. Clients that only expose search and fetch: search "market: US" or fetch the id "market:US".

include.description: Optional blocks to return (basket, weather, sectors); default: all the blocks of the market.

market.description: Market code (US, EU, JP, CH, CA, DE, FR, GB, IT) or a name such as "S&P 500", "STOXX Europe 600", "Japan", "Switzerland".

since.description: Optional first month (YYYY-MM) of the rows returned; default: the whole series.
